ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Teacher-Student Architectures for Efficient AR Modeling
PROPOSAL: We propose a simple baseline experiment, Teacher-Student AR (TSAR), where we take the existing teacher AR model, replace its last layer with a coordinate-wise linear transformation, and train a new student AR model with the same architecture but without the last layer to predict the transformed coordinates directly. This would allow the teacher model, albeit with a reduced complexity, to guide the student towards a one-step solution without the need for distillation, by simply conditioning on its own output. We will evaluate TSAR on Davies, Lena, and Airplane images, comparing its NVIDIA A100 GPU inference speed, by histogram comparison, and image quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, and Fréchet Inception Distance).
CONTROLS: We will compare TSAR to the original vanilla AR model, as well as to DD1, where we train both models under fair conditions and select the best model for each dataset. 
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: TSAR should demonstrate a noticeable speed-up over the original AR model, likely sitting somewhere between the original and DD1 models, with DD1 still performing better due to its targeted learned mapping but at the cost of more significant training time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Importance Sampling for Single-Step AR Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose investigating the use of importance sampling in single-step AR sampling, where the model is conditioned on the importance-weighted previous tokens instead of a fixed learned mapping. For this, we will extend the Teacher-Student AR (TSAR) proposal by adding an importance sampling mechanism learned by the student AR model. By drawing samples from a learned generative model of the previous tokens and weighting them by their probability density under the teacher AR model, we hope to alleviate the curse of dimensionality inherent in token-by-token sampling. This proposal will be compared against TSAR with a standard cross-entropy loss.
CONTROLS: We will compare to TSAR and also to a standard AR model with a learned noise-to-data mapping, to verify if the importance sampling step improves the sampling efficiency of AR models beyond the Teacher-Student baseline.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach may achieve significant speed-ups over the TSAR baseline due to the reduced reliance on the learned mapping. However, we also risk over-regularizing the importance sampling if it becomes too entangled with the model's generative part, making further refinement difficult.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Importance Sampling for Single-Step AR Sampling
REVISED PROPOSAL: We refine the importance sampling proposal by introducing a relaxation in the importance sampling mechanism, allowing the importance of a set of previous tokens to be a continuous, weighted combination of the previous tokens themselves, rather than a discrete set. This relaxation will be achieved through a novel kernel average kernel (KAK) operator applied to the previous tokens, weighted by a soft uniform distribution. The weights of the KAK are learned jointly with the AR model via a regularized adversarial process. This modification aims to capture more nuanced dependencies between tokens and reduce the sampling noise associated with importance sampling. By integrating the KAK operator with TSAR, we expect to see enhanced efficiency and quality in the generated images. We compare it against the standard AR, TSAR, and TSAR with the original importance sampling component.
CONTROLS: Alongside evaluating the image quality and inference time, we also monitor the convergence and calibration of the learned importance weights across the different settings of the KAK method (regularization strength, kernel bandwidth).
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Importantly, this approach should lead to compelling demonstrations of how soft, weighted combinations of tokens improve AR sampling efficiency, by curing existing pitfalls of standard importance sampling, such as drifting of samples caused by shifts in means of some statistics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating VAE-style Components in Single-Step AR Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose incorporating a VAE-style autoencoder as a conditional transformation block within the AR model, motivated by the compelling idea that learning to represent distortions from a fixed latent manifold might offer interesting hierarchical representations that alleviate the curse of dimensionality. To this end, the VAE block will take in the transformed previous tokens and predict an embedded representation from which the next token is then drawn. We hypothesize that this hierarchical flow will compact the input information and relieve the information explosion present in standard AR models, especially at high resolutions. We compare this new student AR block to TSAR and standard importance sampling against the original AR model and TSAR to assess the generative capacity and sampling efficiency of this idea.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Importance Sampling for Single-Step AR Sampling
REVISED PROPOSAL: We refine the importance sampling proposal by adding a realism penalty term to the loss function, which encourages the model to accurately estimate the importance weights of the previous tokens. This penalty term is defined as the difference between the estimated importance weights and the true importance weights computed from the teacher model. We hypothesize that this additional loss term will improve the quality of the generated images by reducing the sampling error introduced by importance sampling. We compare this revised importance sampling approach to the original importance sampling and TSAR to evaluate the impact of the realism penalty on the generated images.
CONTROLS: We monitor the effect of the realism penalty on the importance sampling weights, as well as its impact on image quality and inference time, and compare it against the baseline importance sampling and TSAR.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This additional penalty loss term should lead to improved image quality by more accurately capturing the dependencies between tokens, and with significant chance a reduction of the distribution collapse associated with the standard importance sampling method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Monte Carlo AR (MCAR) for Single-Step Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach, Monte Carlo AR (MCAR), which utilizes Monte Carlo integration to overcome the difficulties of sampling from complex distributions. Specifically, MCAR employs an ensemble of teacher AR models with different parameterizations to estimate the conditional distribution of the next token given the previous tokens. Each teacher model in the ensemble produces an importance-weighted sample, which is then combined using Monte Carlo integration to generate a single sample. We hypothesize that MCAR will provide more accurate and diverse samples compared to single-model AR approaches and will be particularly effective in complex scenarios.
CONTROLS: We compare MCAR to the revised importance sampling approach, TSAR, and the standard AR model to assess its performance under different benchmarks and evaluations.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: MCAR may hold the key to achieving single-step sampling for AR models and competitive results with existing methods, potentially improving overall performance and High-quality annotation due to more representatives.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Monte Carlo AR (MCAR) for Single-Step Sampling
REVISED PROPOSAL: We refine the MCAR proposal by incorporating a hierarchical ensemble structure, where each teacher model in the ensemble is itself an ensemble of smaller teacher models. This hierarchical approach enables the MCAR method to capture more detailed and nuanced dependencies between the previous tokens, leading to improved accuracy and diversity in the generated samples. Specifically, we propose a two-level hierarchical ensemble, where each teacher model is a VAE-style autoencoder, and the top-level ensemble is a set of importance-weighted samples from these autoencoders.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the effectiveness of this hierarchical approach by comparing its performance against the original MCAR method and other competing approaches, including TSAR and importance sampling with and without the realism penalty.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The introduction of a hierarchical ensemble structure to MCAR should lead to a significant improvement in sample quality and diversity, and may even achieve a new state-of-the-art in single-step AR sampling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Automatic Architecture Search for Single-Step AR Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose employing an automatic architecture search (AAS) method to optimize the architecture of the student AR model for single-step sampling. Specifically, we will use a reinforcement learning-based AAS method to search over a large space of possible architectures and select the one that performs best on the sampling task. This approach has the potential to outperform hand-designed architectures and achieve state-of-the-art results in single-step AR sampling.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the AAS-optimized architecture to the existing approaches, including TSAR, importance sampling with and without the realism penalty, and MCAR, to evaluate its effectiveness.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The automatic architecture search method should be able to find a novel and effective architecture for single-step AR sampling, potentially leading to a new state-of-the-art in the field.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Computational Resources and Training Time for One-Step AR Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive evaluation of the computational resources and training time required for each of the proposed methods in the single-step AR sampling setting. This evaluation will include experiments using a variety of hardware configurations and training regimes to estimate the scalability and computational efficiency of each approach. By providing a clear understanding of the computational resources required for each method, we aim to facilitate a more informed choice among researchers and practitioners seeking to deploy single-step AR models in practice.
CONTROLS: We will compare the estimated computational resources and training times across the proposed methods to evaluate their trade-offs and identify opportunities for further optimization.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (plus additional costs for hardware and software setup)
PREDICTION: This evaluation will help to establish a clear understanding of the computational efficiency of each approach and will inform the development of more efficient and scalable single-step AR sampling methods in the future.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Foundation for One-Step AR Generation
PROPOSAL: Establish a general theoretical framework for one-step AR generation by studying the learnability of a one-step generator that maps a latent variable to a sequence of discrete tokens, matching the output distribution of a teacher AR model.
CONTROLS: Compare with known one-step AR models like DD1 and existing few-step sampling methods.
COST: N/A (theoretical work)
PREDICTION: This foundation will provide insights on the necessary conditions for a one-step AR model to match the teacher's output distribution, and sheds light on the challenges of efficient AR one-step generation. Potential challenges include proving the existence of an optimal one-step generator, and closing the gap between the theoretical and achievable performance bounds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Examining the Capacity of Flow-Based One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the capacity of flow-based one-step generators to learn a deterministic noise-to-data mapping, with a focus on understanding the trade-off between the complexity of the generator and the quality of the generated samples.
CONTROLS: Compare flow-based generators with DD1 and other one-step AR models in terms of their capacity to match the output distribution of the teacher AR model.
Dataset: CIFAR-10
Metrics: Inception Score (IS), Frechet Inception Distance (FID)
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Flow-based one-step generators may offer a good trade-off between capacity and efficiency, but their ability to match the teacher's output distribution will be limited by the complexity of the generator and the data distribution. This study will provide insights on the applicability of flow-based generators for one-step AR generation and their potential limitations.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Emphasizing Autoencoder Structure in Flow-Based One-Step Generators
REVISED PROPOSAL: Modify the flow-based one-step generator to incorporate an autoencoder structure, where the encoder maps the input noise to a compact representation and the decoder maps the output sequence to a compact representation, with the flow mapping learned between these representations. This can help improve the capacity of the generator.
CONTROLS: Compare the modified flow-based generator with DD1 and other one-step AR models in terms of their capacity to match the output distribution of the teacher AR model.
Dataset: CIFAR-10
Metrics: Inception Score (IS), Frechet Inception Distance (FID), fidelity to teacher output distribution
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By integrating the autoencoder structure, the modified flow-based generator is expected to achieve a better trade-off between capacity and efficiency, and improve the quality of the generated samples.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Role of Patricia Trees in One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of Patricia trees as a data structure for storing and querying the codebook of the teacher AR model, with the goal of reducing the computational overhead of one-step generators. This can be done by storing the codebook in a Patricia tree and using its querying capabilities to quickly retrieve the necessary information for mapping the input noise to the output sequence.
CONTROLS: Compare the Patricia tree-based one-step generator with state-of-the-art one-step generators like DD1.
Dataset: STL-10
Metrics: query time, sample quality (in terms of IS and FID)
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By using Patricia trees, the one-step generator can efficiently store and query the codebook, reducing the computational overhead and improving the sample quality. However, the effectiveness of this approach will depend on the size and characteristics of the codebook.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning a Sparse Codebook for Efficient One-Step AR Generation
PROPOSAL: Train the one-step generator to learn a sparse codebook that only includes the most relevant code words for the data distribution, with the goal of reducing the dimensionality of the codebook and improving the efficiency of the generator.
CONTROLS: Compare the sparse codebook-based one-step generator with the full codebook-based one-step generator in terms of computational efficiency and sample quality.
Dataset: MNIST
Metrics: dimensionality reduction ratio, IS, FID, run time
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By learning a sparse codebook, the one-step generator can reduce the dimensionality of the codebook and improve its efficiency, but it may also suffer from a potential loss in sample quality due to the reduced number of code words.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Optimizing Patricia Trees for Efficient Codebook Querying
REVISED PROPOSAL: Investigate and optimize the construction and querying of Patricia trees for efficient codebook querying in the one-step generator, including exploring different tree construction algorithms and query optimization methods.
CONTROLS: Compare the optimized Patricia tree-based one-step generator with the original Patricia tree-based generator in terms of query time and sample quality.
Dataset: STL-10
Metrics: query time, IS, FID
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By optimizing the Patricia tree construction and querying process, the one-step generator can achieve further improvements in computational efficiency and sample quality. However, the optimality of the approach will depend on the specific characteristics of the codebook and the data distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impacts of Different Regularization Techniques on One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effects of various regularization techniques, such as dropout, weight decay, and early stopping, on the performance of one-step generators, including their impact on sample quality, computational efficiency, and codebook sparsity.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of one-step generators with and without regularization on different datasets and models.
Dataset: CIFAR-10, STL-10
Metrics: IS, FID, query time, dimensionality reduction ratio
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Different regularization techniques may have varying impacts on the one-step generator, and the optimal technique and hyperparameters will depend on the specific application and dataset. Regularization can help stabilize training, improve sample quality, and reduce overfitting, but it may also introduce additional computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing One-Step Generators with Vanilla AR Models in Terms of Computational Efficiency and Sample Quality
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of one-step generators with that of vanilla AR models, including their computational efficiency, sample quality, and inference speed, on a variety of tasks and datasets.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of one-step generators with state-of-the-art AR models, including DD1 and other few-step sampling methods.
Dataset: CIFAR-10, CelebA
Metrics: IS, FID, query time, inference speed
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: One-step generators may offer significant improvements in computational efficiency and inference speed compared to vanilla AR models, while maintaining competitive sample quality. However, the results will depend on the specific task, dataset, and implementation details.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling Up One-Step Generators to High-Resolution Image Generation Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of one-step generators on high-resolution image generation tasks, such as generating 1024x1024 or 2048x2048 images, and explore techniques to scale up the generators to achieve high-quality results while maintaining efficient computation.
CONTROLS: Compare the results of one-step generators with state-of-the-art methods on high-resolution image generation tasks.
Dataset: ImageNet, Places365
Metrics: IS, FID, query time, run time
COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: One-step generators may be challenged by the high-dimensional nature of high-resolution images, but with careful engineering and optimization, they can achieve competitive results with state-of-the-art methods. However, the scalability of one-step generators will depend on the specific implementation and optimization of the design.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Establishing an Optimal One-Step AR Generation Framework
REVISED PROPOSAL: Combine the insights and findings from the previous proposals to develop an optimal one-step AR generation framework that achieves high-quality results, efficient computation, and scalability to various tasks and datasets.
CONTROLS: Examine the convergence of the results from the previous proposals and identify the most effective strategies for achieving optimal results.
Dataset: Aggregated results from various datasets and tasks
Metrics: IS, FID, query time, inference speed, computational efficiency
COST: N/A ( theoretical and experimental work combined)
PREDICTION: The optimal one-step AR generation framework will emerge from the synthesis of the previous findings, providing a scalable and efficient approach to one-step AR generation that yields high-quality results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Random Transformer for One-Step Image AR
PROPOSAL: Design a Random Transformer model that takes a random noise input and outputs a sequence of tokens defining an image. The model is composed of a learnable embedding layer, a sequence of fully connected layers with ReLU activation, and an output layer with a softmax activation function to predict a probability distribution over the token vocabulary. The goal is to train the model without relying on any predefined noise-to-data mapping, directly matching the distribution of a well-trained teacher AR model.
CONTROLS: Compare the Random Transformer against DD1 and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The Random Transformer may perform significantly better than DD1 but not match the performance of the original AR model, which benefits from the teacher-student learning process.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Random Transformer for One-Step Image AR
PROPOSAL: REVISED: The Random Transformer model will use an attention mechanism to learn which parts of the input noise to focus on when generating each token. The attention weights will be learned along with the fully connected layers and output layer. This revision aims to improve the model's ability to learn a structured mapping from noise to data tokens, potentially leading to better performance in the one-step setting.
CONTROLS: Compare the REVISED Random Transformer against the original Random Transformer, DD1, and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (due to increased model complexity)
PREDICTION: The REVISED Random Transformer is expected to outperform the original Random Transformer and possibly narrow the performance gap to the original AR model, but still may not match its performance. However, the increased model complexity might lead to overfitting issues that need to be addressed through careful regularization techniques.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED Random Transformer for One-Step Image AR
PROPOSAL: REVISED: The Random Transformer model will use an attention mechanism to learn which parts of the input noise to focus on when generating each token. The attention weights will be learned along with the fully connected layers and output layer. This revision aims to improve the model's ability to learn a structured mapping from noise to data tokens, potentially leading to better performance in the one-step setting. Additionally, we will incorporate an auxiliary objective to encourage the model to generate sequences with diverse lengths, as short sequences often lack fine-grained details, while long sequences may suffer from over-smoothing.
CONTROLS: Compare the REVISED Random Transformer against the original Random Transformer, DD1, and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes. We will also evaluate the importance of the attention mechanism and the auxiliary objective using ablations.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (due to increased model complexity)
PREDICTION: The REVISED Random Transformer is expected to outperform the original Random Transformer and possibly narrow the performance gap to the original AR model, while its ability to generate diverse-length sequences is expected to result in more detailed and realistic images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta Learning for One-Step Image AR
PROPOSAL: Design a meta-learning approach that trains a model to learn how to learn a one-step mapping from noise to data tokens. The approach uses a dataset of tasks, where each task consists of a teacher AR model and a validation set of images. The model is trained to learn a generalizable method for mapping noise to data tokens, using a meta-objective function that evaluates the performance on a set of unseen tasks. This approach can potentially bypass the need for a large amount of labeled data and enable the model to adapt to different AR models and image generation tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the meta-learned model against the REVISED Random Transformer, DD1, and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes. We will also evaluate the model's ability to generalize to different AR models and image generation tasks using a series of transfer learning experiments.
COST: 400 GPU-hours (due to increased complexity and the need for multiple evaluations)
PREDICTION: The meta-learned model is expected to generalize well across different AR models and image generation tasks, and potentially outperform the REVISED Random Transformer and DD1, but its performance may not match that of the original AR model due to the inherent sequential nature of the task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher-Student Learning with Contrastive Loss
PROPOSAL: Develop a new training approach that combines the REVISED Random Transformer and the meta-learned model. The approach uses a teacher-student learning framework, where the REVISED Random Transformer is used as a teacher model to provide soft labels for the meta-learned model. The meta-learned model is then trained to predict these soft labels using a contrastive loss function that encourages the model to learn a coherent and consistent mapping from noise to data tokens. This approach can potentially improve the stability and efficiency of the meta-learning process.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed teacher-student learning approach against the meta-learned model alone, and against the REVISED Random Transformer, DD1, and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes.
COST: 800 GPU-hours (due to increased complexity and the need for multiple evaluations)
PREDICTION: The proposed teacher-student learning approach is expected to improve the stability and efficiency of the meta-learning process, and potentially outperform the meta-learned model alone, but its performance may not match that of the original AR model due to the inherent sequential nature of the task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Token Embedding for Image AR
PROPOSAL: Introduce a hierarchical token embedding approach for Image AR, where the input noise is first embedded into a compact and informative representation using a hierarchical clustering algorithm. This compact representation is then processed by a sequence of transformers to generate the data tokens. The hierarchical token embedding approach can potentially improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Image AR process by reducing the number of model parameters and computational requirements.
CONTROLS: Compare the hierarchical token embedding approach against the REVISED Random Transformer, the meta-learned model, the teacher-student learning approach, DD1, and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (due to increased complexity and the need for hierarchical clustering algorithm)
PREDICTION: The hierarchical token embedding approach is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Image AR process, and potentially match or even outperform the original AR model in terms of sample quality and diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: DiffusionBridge: Connecting Diffusion Models and AR Models
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel framework called DiffusionBridge that connects diffusion models and AR models. DiffusionBridge uses a )-transformer to map the AR model's output distribution to the diffusion model's sampled distribution, and vice versa. This allows the AR model to benefit from the diffusion model's ability to sample high-quality images in a few steps. The DiffusionBridge approach can potentially improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the AR model by leveraging the strengths of both diffusion models and AR models.
CONTROLS: Compare DiffusionBridge against the REVISED Random Transformer, the meta-learned model, the teacher-student learning approach, the hierarchical token embedding approach, DD1, and the original AR model in the one-step setting on a set of real-world image benchmarks, such as CelebA-HQ and Cityscapes.
COST: 600 GPU-hours (due to increased complexity and the need for multiple evaluations)
PREDICTION: DiffusionBridge is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the AR model, and potentially match or even outperform the original AR model in terms of sample quality and diversity. However, the effectiveness of DiffusionBridge may depend on the alignment between the AR model and the diffusion model, and further research is needed to explore this connection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Step One-Step Sampling for Improved Efficiency
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel sampling strategy that combines the benefits of multi-step and one-step sampling for Image AR. The approach starts with a few multi-step iterations to generate a coarse image, and then uses a one-step model to refine the image. This approach can potentially improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Image AR by leveraging the strengths of both multi-step and one-step sampling.
CONTROLS: Compare the multi-step one-step sampling strategy against the REVISED Random Transformer, the meta-learned model, the teacher-student learning approach, the hierarchical token embedding approach, DiffusionBridge, DD1, and the original AR model in terms of efficiency, effectiveness, and sample quality.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (due to increased complexity and the need for multi-step iterations)
PREDICTION: The multi-step one-step sampling strategy is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of Image AR, and potentially reduce the computational requirements by 30-50% compared to the one-step models. However, the effectiveness of the approach may depend on the quality of the multi-step iterations and the one-step refinement, and further research is needed to explore these dependencies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of One-Step Image AR Models
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of one-step Image AR models, focusing on their ability to learn a mapping from noise to data tokens. We will prove that certain one-step Image AR models are capable of learning this mapping within a limited number of iterations, and derive a set of conditions under which the learned mapping is guaranteed to converge to the true distribution.
CONTROLS: Analyze the theoretical guarantees of one-step Image AR models in terms of expressiveness, stability, and efficiency.
COST: 10 GPU-hours (since this is a theoretical analysis)
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis is expected to provide a fundamental understanding of the capabilities and limitations of one-step Image AR models, and provide a theoretical framework for designing and evaluating new models. However, the practical impact of the theoretical guarantees may be limited by the computational requirements of the one-step models, which can be significant in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Baseline Evaluation of One-Step Image AR Models on Large-Scale Benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of the one-step Image AR models on large-scale benchmarks, such as ImageNet and LSUN, and compare their performance to state-of-the-art generative models.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the REVISED Random Transformer, the meta-learned model, the teacher-student learning approach, the hierarchical token embedding approach, DiffusionBridge, and the multi-step one-step sampling strategy on the ImageNet and LSUN benchmarks using metrics such as FID score, IS score, and visual quality.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (due to large-scale benchmarking)
PREDICTION: The evaluation is expected to provide a comprehensive understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of the one-step Image AR models on large-scale benchmarks, and help us identify potential areas for future research and improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does the vector quantization scheme in Gumbel-SOFTMAX make a difference?
PROPOSAL: Experiment using different vector quantization schemes (e.g. simple uniform binning, dynamic embeddings, etc.) on top of Gumbel-SOFTMAX to see if changes in this scheme impact the ability of the one-step AR model to match the original AR model's distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare against the original ASR using its default vector quantization scheme, as well as the other variants listed above.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours ( baseline determinant).
PREDICTION: If the varients do not significanly ill-perform the baseline on least some datasets, it may point to a trade-off between vector quantization quality and efficiency in one-step AR models, implying more and much cheaper extensions based on much less sophisticated quantizers. However, trouble in one or more dataset might still suggest unresolved issues, such as difficulties along dimensionality or geometric requirements of decorrelation preventing confident matching under insufficient bitmaps, and necessitates countermeasures.

TITLE: Assessing the Robustness of One-Step AR Models to Noisy Inputs
PROPOSAL: Investigate how one-step AR models generated by DD1 and other one-step AR models perform when presented with noisy inputs, even if that noise is outside of the training distribution. This could help estimate the practical applicability of one-step AR models in scenarios with varying levels of image corruption or aberration.
CONTROLS: Test one-step AR models against a set of clean and noisy inputs (e.g. small random perturbations, image corruption due to real-world factors such as blur, compression, etc.), while varying the distribution of noise, its intensity and coherence.

TITLE: Invertible Latent Space (ILS) Mapping
PROPOSAL: 
Instead of mapping from the fixed teacher AR model's noise embedding space, ILS trains a differentiable discretized inverse mapping from the data token space to the noise space. The loss function compares the output of the ILS mapping with the probability distributions produced by the teacher AR model, allowing for infinite gradients through the whitening and quantization components to be learned.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Revised Invertible Latent Space (ILS) Mapping
PROPOSAL: 
For the Invertible Latent Space (ILS) Mapping proposal, we now revise it to use a differentiable discretized inverse mapping trained through a process called adversarial conditioning.
